answer: The finisher rubs his barrel with linseed oil, and the rub must bring up a shine without hiding the grain. Keg beech cask charrer chestnut seal is the rubbing: a seal beech cask charrers carry after charring pit hearings. The tide is the first rub, made at the bench; the signal is the last, made before the barrel is shipped, and the copper is the cloth itself, dark with oil. A counterfeiter faces 13 false rubs and 13 false cloths.
